newsitem.title: USA: U.S. officials call Russian missile comment absurd.
newsitem.headline: U.S. officials call Russian missile comment absurd.

text.p: U.S. officials described as absurd a Russian statement on Thursday suggesting it was Washington and not Moscow which had blocked signature of an agreement on regional missile defences.
The State Department announced Wednesday that the signing ceremony, which was to have been held in Geneva Thursday, had been called off and accused Russia of reversing its position.
But Russia expressed "surprise and regret" at the postponement of the deal and clearly implied that the United States was to blame.
"The statement this morning is absurd, frankly, from the Russian foreign ministry, saying that we didn't want to sign. They didn't want to sign," said a U.S. official who asked not to be identified.

The agreement announced last month by U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher and Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov would specify which short-range systems are allowed under the 1972 Anti-Ballistic Missile (ABM) treaty.
But it covers only lower-speed anti-missile systems, leaving faster systems to be negotiated later in a part two agreement.
Russian Foreign Ministry spokesman Mikhail Demurin said Moscow was ready to sign the missile deal documents "if they are properly prepared."
But he indicated Russia wanted deputy foreign ministers to review progress on the part two agreement first, adding that Russia's Georgy Mamedov had flown to Geneva with this in view.

"What the Russians have effectively done here is try to merge elements of part one and part two which, of course, is contrary to the joint statement that was issued in late September," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns.
"That's the problem here. The Russians were not willing to go ahead today in Geneva and sign the part one documents."
"What we would like to do is convince them that we need to go back to the September agreement, sign those documents, keep on negotiating on part two, keep this process going," he said.

Russia has long been suspicious of U.S. plans to develop regional missile defences, fearing they are intended to circumvent the ABM treaty which is widely considered a cornerstone of international arms control.
